Simon — thanks for the clear breakdown. I put together a short brief (attached) and summarize the pragmatic recommendation below so you can paste into procurement. High-level TL;DR: use a mixed pool with L4s for cheap, high-throughput short-context traffic and embeddings; H100s reserved for large-context models and peak heavy-generation; A100s can be used as a middle ground if you need more VRAM per-slot without H100 pricing.

Key tradeoffs (short):
- Memory (OOM risk): H100 (80 GB HBM) > A100 (40/80 GB variants) > L4 (24 GB typical). If your 64k-token pipelines require large KV caches, prioritize H100 for those slots; otherwise A100 80GB is an acceptable fallback.
- Latency / throughput: L4 optimized for cost-per-token on short requests + embeddings — often highest throughput and lowest cost at small batch sizes. H100 shines for long-sequence throughput and models that benefit from tensor-core FP16/TF32 kernels (and large KV cache efficiency). A100 is capable but generally higher cost per token than L4 for short bursts and lower max efficiency than H100 for massive seq lengths.
- Quantization and model size: If you plan to run quantized 4/8-bit variants, L4 and A100 both handle int8 paths well. H100 gives better headroom for mixed-precision kernels and large-weight models without aggressive quantization.
- Failure modes / operational notes:
  - Long-context OOM: L4 slots will OOM on largest contexts; route those requests to H100 or A100-80GB.
  - Tail latency: Use autoscaling + overprovisioning headroom for L4 frontends to avoid queueing; H100s can be fewer but provisioned for sustained long jobs.
  - Cost spikes: Nightly batch summarization should be scheduled to use preemptible/burst capacity if possible or routed to a low-cost A100 pool.

Phased SKU plan (recommended):
1) Phase 1 (0–3 months) — Proof + baseline:
   - Deploy L4 pool sized for 120 short req/s steady-state, configurable burst to 200 via autoscale.
   - Reserve 4 H100 slots for long-context and heavy generation canaries (handles the 64k windows).
   - Use A100 (40GB) spot-like burst capacity for nightly batch to reduce cost.
2) Phase 2 (3–9 months) — Scale and stabilize:
   - Add A100 80GB slots if long-context usage grows beyond reserved H100 capacity.
   - Increase L4 pool and enable KV prefix caching + batching for embeddings to reduce token spend.
3) Phase 3 (9+ months) — Cost optimization and consolidation:
   - Evaluate quantized model variants to migrate more traffic to L4 / A100 with lower unit cost.
   - Convert some H100 reserve to a smaller H100 cluster only for peak long-context requirements; keep most latency-sensitive short chaff on L4.

Procurement/ops answers:
- Lead times: typical procurement for Dedicated reserved capacity is 4–8 weeks from contract to allocation for standard SKUs; specialized H100 capacity can push to 6–12 weeks depending on region. We'll coordinate with infra partners and provide an expected schedule once we sign.
- Mixed-SKU pools & fallbacks: Redwood supports multi-SKU pools and routing policies — you can set routing by model, request size, or latency target. Fallbacks to compatible model variants (e.g., A100-80 fallback to H100 when available) are supported.

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll share the attached one-page brief and a populated sizing workbook (use your lumena_ops_sizing_v2.xlsx) with the numbers filled in.
- Quick ops call (30 minutes) this week to agree on initial counts and timelines.

Attaching: redwood_capacity_brief.pdf (one-page summary)
